headline: Record AUM and fee earnings; GAAP results stay volatile

summary_short: TPG's AUM rose 25% y/y to $326.8 billion and Fee-Related Earnings grew 43% y/y to $314.6 million in Q2 FY2026, while GAAP net income attributable to TPG Inc. swung to $93 million from a $1.5 million loss in Q1, driven mainly by mark-to-market performance allocations.
summary_long: AUM grew 25% y/y to $326.8 billion on $60.7 billion of trailing-twelve-month capital raised, partly offset by $26.4 billion of realizations; FAUM rose 24% to $181.0 billion. Fee-Related Earnings rose 43% y/y to $314.6 million ($0.82/share, +28% q/q). GAAP net income attributable to TPG Inc. of $93 million (basic EPS $0.44) swung from a $1.5 million Q1 net loss, driven by mark-to-market capital allocation-based income and performance allocation compensation, both highly variable. Pre-tax Distributable Earnings rose 6.5% y/y to $296.5 million; the board declared a $0.59/share dividend, flat q/q. Cash rose 11% q/q to $944.7 million; long-term debt was flat at $2,343.7 million.

drivers.explanation: CEO Jon Winkelried called it a record first half of 2026, citing the diversified, growing franchise, investment performance, and expanding client relationships across the platform.
Growth driven by $60.7B of trailing-12-month capital raised — including $12.3B in TPG X and $9.3B in TPG Direct Lending — partially offset by $26.4B of realizations, per the release.
Growth driven by $25.7B of fee-earning capital raised (including $11.9B in TPG X, $1.7B in THP III) and $25.0B of deployment; realizations were $13.8B, per the release.
Growth is driven almost entirely by capital allocation-based income (fund mark-to-market), which rose to $1,136.5M from $351.5M a year ago; fees and other revenue grew a steadier 24% to $705.0M.

drivers.explanation: Rose on higher consolidated Fee-Related Earnings plus a slightly larger allocated share to TPG Inc. (43% vs 42% in Q1) and a higher record-date share count.
Roughly flat q/q as the rise in Fee-Related Earnings was largely offset by lower realized performance allocations, net ($35.4M vs $67.7M in Q1), per the reconciliation table.

The shard's sourceLink pointed at the 8-K cover document (tpg-20260804.htm); scripts/resolve-edgar-exhibit.mjs correctly resolved it to the EX-99.1 press release first, avoiding a wasted fetch on the cover stub. GAAP revenue and net income for an alternative asset manager like TPG are structurally noisy: 'Total revenues' includes capital allocation-based income, an unrealized mark-to-market line that swung from $351.5M (2Q'25) to $1,136.5M (2Q'26), and 'Total compensation and benefits' includes performance allocation compensation that moves in lockstep ($233.4M to $776.7M). This mechanically drives large GAAP revenue/EPS/net-income swings that are not comparable period-to-period the way an operating company's would be — the company's own non-GAAP metrics (Fee-Related Earnings, Distributable Earnings, After-tax DE) are designed to strip this volatility out and are what management and the dividend policy are actually built on. EPS (basic/diluted) q/q and diluted EPS y/y deltas are reported as 'NM' because the prior-period base was negative or near-zero; net income attributable to TPG Inc. y/y (+525.4%) is a real percentage (prior base $14.9M was not near-zero) but is still driven almost entirely by the mark-to-market swing described above. FRE-per-share and After-tax-DE-per-share y/y deltas are omitted: the supplement's 'FRE, After-Tax DE, and Dividends' table shows only the trailing two quarters (1Q'26, 2Q'26), so no same-basis 2Q'25 comparison figure was available. AUM q/q growth (+6.7%) was derived arithmetically from the AUM Rollforward table's quarter-beginning ($306,182M) and quarter-end ($326,777M) balances; the release states AUM and FAUM y/y growth (+25%, +24%) directly, which reconciles with the rollforward's twelve-month-ended figures. No forward guidance (revenue, EPS, capex, or otherwise) was disclosed in either exhibit; the guidance array is intentionally left empty. Extended metrics (dividend per share, AUM, FAUM, FRE/share, After-tax DE/share) were extracted from the same two exhibits at 0.95-0.98 confidence via scripts/apply-extended-metrics.mjs; the registry's 'financials' sector-specific set (NIM, efficiency ratio, CET1, ROTCE, net charge-off ratio, deposits, provision for credit losses) is bank-specific and does not apply to an alternative asset manager, so those fields were omitted rather than force-fit, and the four TPG-specific metrics above were captured instead as the sector's actual decision-relevant KPIs. No stock buyback, capex, or asset-sale figures were disclosed in either exhibit.
